newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya says exiled Moslem preacher free to return.
newsitem.headline: Kenya says exiled Moslem preacher free to return.

text.p: Kenya said on Thursday that Sheikh Khalid Balala, a Moslem preacher and leading critic of Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi, was free to return to the country after two years of forced exile in Germany.
In a dramatic move, attorney-general Amos Wako said the government had reversed its earlier stand not to allow the fiery preacher back home after accusing him of being a Yemeni.

Moi and Kenyan immigration officials have said Balala, who has a Kenyan mother and Yemeni father, automatically gave up his Kenyan citizenship when he failed to renounce his Yemeni citizenship at the age of 21.
Wako said the government move followed appeals from many quarters, including the Balala family and the Moslem community.

"The government has allowed Balala to return so he can sort out his various problems. He will return as soon as he makes an application for travel documents at our embassy in Bonn or our consulate in Frankfurt," Wako said.
Analysts said the return of Balala, who commands a large following in Kenya's coastal region, is a major boost for the country's opposition in presidential and parliamentary elections this year.

Last week, Balala speaking from his exile base in Frankfurt, threatened to launch a wave of popular unprisings and industrial unrest in Kenya if Moi, seeking re-election this year, did not agree to step down.

Balala had also threatened to enter the country illegally and wage an armed struggle to bring down Moi's government, which he accuses of being an oppressive regime and likens to that of ousted Zairean dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
Balala was refused entry to Kenya on June 7. Security officers detained him as he arrived at the coastal resort of Mombasa aboard an airliner from Frankfurt and forced him to return to Germany.
He said his Kenyan passport had expired while he was in Germany but the Kenyan embassy in Bonn refused to renew it. He said he had German travel documents but remained a Kenyan citizen.
President Moi, aged 73 and in power since 1978, must call elections in 1997 pitting the ruling KANU party against an opposition fractured mainly along ethnic and personal lines.
The opposition has called for peaceful rallies across the country on Monday to press for constitutional reforms Moi has refused to carry out.
Earlier last month, one person was killed and scores of shops in the Kenyan capital of Nairobi were looted during rioting after security forces broke up an opposition rally.
